blocks.md: This lesson follows **Worker Failure Mid-Trajectory** in *Durable Execution* (Vol III).

blocks.source: Vol III, Durable Execution, § Worker Failure Mid-Trajectory
blocks.md: Consider a software repair agent (a later section) that has admitted and dispatched an integration test against `ws_r18`, a fixed workspace snapshot of candidate patch `r18`. Before the test runner reports a result, the worker process crashes, or the host suffers a spot preemption (the sudden reclamation of an ephemeral cloud node). A replacement worker cannot simply re-invoke the model with the original prompt.

blocks.prompt: Think first: In two or three sentences, explain why Record and replay matters for the system this section describes.
blocks.md: Compare your answer with the book's claim: A sampled model reply cannot be regenerated, so reproduction substitutes recorded inputs at nondeterministic boundaries, and one recording serves time-travel inspection, harness regression, and counterfactual branching.

questions.q: The section **Worker Failure Mid-Trajectory** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: Young's interval prices checkpoints when a crash loses work to re-execute, and once each turn is logged the stride lengthens by the square root of the cost ratio because a crash costs reconstruction, not resampling.
An acknowledgment is durable only against the faults its storage tier survives, so each write's durability is declared against a failure domain rather than assumed.

A sampled model reply cannot be regenerated, so reproduction substitutes recorded inputs at nondeterministic boundaries, and one recording serves time-travel inspection, harness regression, and counterfactual branching.
Debugging two executions steps boundary by boundary from a verified checkpoint to the first mismatch under a declared equivalence, because every later difference may be a consequence.
